title: Portage deployment registry
description: One entry per LiteLLM deployment. src/portage/render_config.py validates portage-local/registry.yaml (or config/profiles/*.example.registry.yaml) against this schema before rendering. See HB-0-gateway-foundation.md Step 1.

alias.description: One of the seven fixed capability aliases (HB-0 'Fixed decisions'). No others are valid — the ladder is closed by design.

provider_route.description: The LiteLLM provider prefix this entry renders under (e.g. 'ollama_chat/<model_id>'). 'ollama_chat', never 'ollama' — HB-0 fixed decision. 'deepseek', 'morph' and 'moonshot' are native LiteLLM providers, verified present in the pinned v1.93.0 (api.deepseek.com/beta, api.morphllm.com/v1, api.moonshot.ai/v1) — first-party routes, per CW-04 §2.2's serving-precision rule. NOTE the two OpenAI-shaped routes are NOT interchangeable: 'openai' is the Scale-2 institution-hosted vLLM path (SOVEREIGN_BASE_URL/SOVEREIGN_TOKEN), while 'openai_direct' is first-party api.openai.com (OPENAI_API_KEY, no api_base). Rendering GPT-5.6 Sol under 'openai' would have pointed it at the sovereign endpoint and signed it with the sovereign token.

model_id.description: The model identifier without the provider prefix, e.g. 'qwen3-coder:7b' or 'z-ai/glm-5.2'.

endpoint.description: Required for provider_route: ollama_chat; optional and honored for provider_route: openai (an institution-hosted vLLM base URL at Scale 2). Always an os.environ/ reference — never a literal hostname, IP or URL, and never a secret value — so the registry stays portable across machines and deployments. Env var names are per-deployment namespaces: SOVEREIGN_BASE_URL resolves to the Jetstream2 endpoint in the EduCloud deployment and is parked in Line P's. Enforced in render_config.py, not pure JSON Schema, since it's conditional on provider_route.

order.description: Failover order within this alias's deployment group. Required when an alias has more than one enabled entry (checked in render_config.py, since JSON Schema can't see sibling array items).

license.description: The model's license class (e.g. 'Apache-2.0', 'MIT'). Use the literal string 'UNVERIFIED' when the license hasn't been confirmed yet — never guess a specific license name. This field is the human-readable grant name; the machine-checkable gate is `license_family`.

license_family.description: CW-04 §2.5 (C6). The allowlist class `open_weight_only` tests against. `open_weight: true` is NOT sufficient on its own — Kimi K3 ships public weights under a bespoke grant with a revenue-triggered separate-agreement clause and a UI attribution mandate, so weight availability does not imply an acceptable license. That falsification is why this field exists. `unverified` is the honest value when the grant has not been read; it is deliberately NOT allowlist-eligible, so an unread license fails closed rather than passing on the strength of published weights.

thinking_disabled_for_structured.description: Optional. True when this deployment must have thinking/reasoning turned off for structured/JSON/tool calls (e.g. Gemma 4 E4B per HB-0 Step 1). Absent means not applicable.

stream_tools.description: Optional. Set to false by HB-0 Step 4 (tests/test_toolcalls.py) if this deployment's tool calls work non-streaming but fail to reconstruct correctly under stream: true. Absent means untested or known-good under both.

effort.description: Optional Lane-B counterpart to models.json's Lane-A `effort`. Renders to LiteLLM's `reasoning_effort` param. Null or absent means no effort control — the flag is omitted entirely rather than sent as a default, matching failup.py's tiers-file rule that 'default' is not a valid effort. Lets one checkpoint occupy two rungs at different reasoning budgets (CC-P6 §3: DeepSeek V4 Flash, then the same checkpoint at max effort, before the fable tier). Caveat for whoever boots this: litellm_settings.yaml sets drop_params: true, so a provider that does not accept reasoning_effort silently drops it and the max-effort rung collapses into a duplicate of the rung below it. Confirm acceptance at Gate 2 rather than assuming the rung is live.

fable_tier.description: Optional, default false. Marks a rung that ordinary fail-up escalation must never select — reachable only when a human explicitly declares this specific task warrants it, with the reason logged (CW-02 §3's logged-reason requirement for the proprietary lines). Absent or false means an ordinary rung. This is a DECLARATIVE marker, exactly like `enabled` and exactly like CW-02's T6 gate, which is policy plus `enabled: false` and not code — see the CC-P6 report. It is not read by failup.py, which escalates through .claude/tiers.json and never opens this registry.

failover_only.description: Optional, default false. CW-04 §2.2: a route that is availability insurance, not a capability rung — reachable only when a first-party endpoint health-checks down, never entering a benchmark cell. OpenRouter is the case this exists for. Nothing in the Scale-1 registry sets it yet and that is deliberate: any row rendered into a model group is routable by LiteLLM's own retry/fallback, so a `failover_only` row placed in a live alias group would be exactly the routable rung CW-04 demoted it from. The health-check-gated call path and the `unbenched` tag are HB-2 (CW-04 §8 item 6); this field is the schema affordance waiting for them.

data_classification.description: CW02-decisions.md D15's enum. Full enforcement is HB-2 scope; the field exists at HB-0 so the registry doesn't need a breaking schema change later.

benchmark_version.description: Which BFCLv3/IFEval run this row's numbers came from, e.g. a dated harness run or a cited public leaderboard snapshot. Null when bfclv3/ifeval are both null.

bfclv3.description: Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard v3 score. Selection rule (HB-0 Step 1): any sub-4B model doing tool/function calls needs ~50+ here. Null means not yet measured — never fabricate a number.

ifeval.description: IFEval instruction-following score. Null means not yet measured.

enabled.description: false entries still render into model_list, carrying `enabled: false` in model_info — they are NOT excluded. HB-0 Gate 2 requires /v1/models to list every alias the deployment declares, so dropping a disabled row would hide an alias entirely; downstream tooling (failup.py, herdr-meters) filters on model_info.enabled instead. proprietary_code/proprietary_research exist disabled so HB-2's rescue path flips a flag rather than adding config. To make a deployment genuinely unreachable — the Scale-2 student lane's requirement — REMOVE the row from that lane's registry; `enabled: false` is not an isolation mechanism.
